text:
Kevin R: heads-up — found a perf regression on recent canary when serving Llama-4x at seqlen 1536. microbench shows fallback to the generic attention kernel instead of the SM92-tensorcore path.  ~3.6x slower for long sequences :eyes:

Anna R: can you paste the probe output and the exact flags used?

Kevin R: repro steps: run profile probe on cluster node (nv 538, SM 92 hw). command: `./runtime/probe_gpu --json --kernels`

```
GPU: NVIDIA A800 (sm=92)
Driver: 538.13
Detected features: tensor_cores=true, bf16=true, fp8=false
Chosen kernels: attention_generic, matmul_generic
Autotune log: selected path=generic (reason=seqlen>1024 && kernel_score_generic>kernel_score_tensorcore by 1.2)
Profile: attention_generic p50=6.2ms p90=12.1ms tokens/s=98
Microbench tensorcore path (cached): p50=1.7ms p90=3.2ms tokens/s=360
```

Kevin R: seems detection flagged fp8=false, but hw supports fp8 on this driver — mismatch due to our fp8 probe (cuda kernel) returning 0 when running under container with old libc. that toggles the kernel scoring to avoid fp8/tc kernels.

Sarah (ML): that matches KV-cache degradation we saw — when attention kernel falls back, KV layout changes and batching amplifier kicks in, increasing memory copies. we've seen batching heuristics add extra padding when seqlen path != expected.

Mike O: timeline? did this roll go out to dedicated nodes or only canary? any incidents reported?

Kevin R: only canary yesterday (10:33 UTC). alert from perf-agent: sustained latency spike on /generate for customer A at 11:05. autoscaler didn't trigger since CPU looked fine.

Julia P: proposed mitigation: add two runtime capability flags — `force_tensor_cores` and `allow_fp8_probe_override`. default false. operator can set per-deployment. patch snippet for config: 

```
{
  "runtime_flags": {
    "force_tensor_cores": false,
    "allow_fp8_probe_override": true,
    "seqlen_tensorcore_threshold": 1024
  }
}
```

Julia P: also propose minor autotune rule change: when probe says fw-driver mismatch (probe returns inconsistent bits across runs), prefer conservative tensorcore_score boost and schedule a short microbench to validate before switching to generic kernel.

Kevin R: test script I used to validate workaround: `./runtime/bench_attention --mode=tensorcore --seqlen=1536 --iters=200` (runs in ~90s). autotune-bot posted the microbench:

```
autotune-bot: microbench result: node=node-17A, mode=tensorcore, seqlen=1536, p50=1.8ms, p90=3.3ms, success=true
```

autotune-bot: note: if container libc blocks fp8 probe, the quick microbench validates capability despite probe false negative.

Anna R: long-term we should harden the fp8 probe: run small kernel that exercises fp8 path and check output entropy rather than syscall-level capability bits. fallback: run microbench automatically when score delta > 1.0 for seqlen > seqlen_threshold.

Sarah (ML): agree. also need to adjust KV cache prefetcher when kernel path toggles: avoid repadding active batches mid-request. patch idea: tag cached KV entries with kernel_path_id; on kernel switch, keep serving in-flight requests with old path and warm new path for new requests. reduces thrash.

Mike O: ops action: roll canary back? or flip `allow_fp8_probe_override` on canary nodes to true, run microbench sweep across regions, then roll to dedicated if stable.

Kevin R: I'll open PR for probe hardening + config flags. will attach benchmark logs and a small ffmpeg-sized summary for SLO review. tagging @Anna R for review. :thumbsup:

Anna R: thanks — please include a reproducible container image + exact driver/kernel used. I'll review autotune rule change on Friday.

Julia P: forwarding note: add telemetry event when kernel_path changes at runtime (include seqlen, model, kernel_id) so we can alert earlier.

Kevin R: ack. I'll add telemetry and a short dashboard query for frequency of `kernel_path != preferred_tensorcore` across seqlen buckets.

Mike O: thanks team. if anyone sees regressions ping #incidents.
